run.question: The payment-api pod in namespace app-259 had issues on November 23, 2026 around 13:45 UTC. What happened?

report.summary: Only the Loki log source responded in this Run; the Kubernetes API, Prometheus and Jaeger all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so pod status, events, owner objects, ConfigMaps, metrics and traces could not be checked (gaps below). The available logs show the single pod payment-api-259-d8f7b9c4-abc12 in namespace app-259 (labels job=payment-api, service=payment-api) changing behaviour at about 13:46 UTC on 2026-11-23: from 13:46 to 14:44 it emitted 8 ERROR lines 'Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted' with queue_length 5-15 and wait_time_ms 1227-4840, whereas the returned lines from 11:19 to 13:42 were only 'Payment processed successfully', and successful payments reappear at 14:49 and 15:27. The observed symptom is therefore an exhausted database connection pool inside the payment-api pod with payment-processing failures roughly 13:46-14:44 UTC, after which error logging stopped. What saturated the pool (a pool-size configuration change, a slow/unavailable database, or extra load) is not established: no ConfigMap, pod-status, event, ReplicaSet/Deployment or trace evidence was obtainable, so no root-cause object is named.

claims.text: Pod payment-api-259-d8f7b9c4-abc12 (labels namespace=app-259, job=payment-api, service=payment-api) logged ERROR 'Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted' at 13:46 (wait_time_ms 1227, queue_length 10), 13:54 (2104, 11), 14:03 (1495, 8), 14:15 (2965, 9), 14:19 (4005, 10), 14:21 (4840, 8), 14:31 (2358, 15) and 14:44 (3836, 5) UTC on 2026-11-23.

In the 10:00-13:45 UTC window on 2026-11-23 the returned log lines for {namespace="app-259"} were all level INFO 'Payment processed successfully' (11:19, 11:40, 11:44, 12:57, 13:42), and the level=ERROR count_over_time series for that namespace begins at 2026-11-23T13:46:11, its earliest returned point in the sampled 11:00-16:28 range.

Error logging from the pod stops after the 14:44 UTC line: in the 14:30-16:28 window the samples are the two 14:31 and 14:44 ERROR lines followed by level INFO 'Payment processed successfully' at 14:49 (PAY-8206) and 15:27 (PAY-4120), and the level=ERROR series' last returned sample is at 2026-11-23T14:47:47.

The only log stream found in namespace app-259 belongs to a single pod, payment-api-259-d8f7b9c4-abc12, under job=payment-api; a count_over_time grouped by job and pod_name returned only that one series, and a count grouped by namespace for {namespace=~".+"} returned only namespace app-259.

All returned log lines for this namespace carry the same pod name payment-api-259-d8f7b9c4-abc12 (ReplicaSet hash segment d8f7b9c4) from 11:19 through 15:27 UTC, so the logs contain no evidence of a pod-name change during the window; pod identity, restarts and owner objects could not be verified because the Kubernetes API was unavailable in this Run.

The immediate failure mechanism is saturation of payment-api's own database connection pool: acquisition waits of 1227-4840 ms with 5-15 requests queued are exactly what the ERROR text reports, so payment processing failed while waiting for a pool slot rather than on an application-level validation error.

Candidate cause not tested: a configuration change to payment-api's database pool (for example a reduced maximum pool size), which would fit a burst starting at 13:46 and stopping at 14:44 with no pod-name change, but no ConfigMap, Deployment, ReplicaSet or event object was readable in this Run, so this remains unverified.

Second candidate cause not tested: degradation of the database dependency itself (slow or unreachable database) holding connections until the pool was exhausted; no database service, endpoint, RPC or trace evidence was available, so this is unresolved and is not claimed as impact on any dependency.

Against an ongoing outage on this pod: after the last ERROR at 14:44 UTC the pod logged successful payments at 14:49 and 15:27, and the level=ERROR series' last returned point is 2026-11-23T14:47:47, so the failure window observable in logs is bounded to roughly 13:46-14:44.

A pod replacement visible in application logs is not supported: the same pod name payment-api-259-d8f7b9c4-abc12 appears in every returned line from 11:19 to 15:27 UTC; container state, restart counts and termination reasons themselves could not be read because the Kubernetes API was unavailable.

gaps: Kubernetes API was unreachable for every call in this Run (kubernetes_jq_query, kubernetes_tabular_query, kubernetes_count, fetch_pod_logs all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so pod phase, readiness, restart counts, container last-termination reason/exit code, events across all namespaces, ReplicaSet/Deployment ownership and ConfigMap contents for payment-api could not be checked.

Prometheus was unreachable for every call (get_metric_names, get_all_labels, get_prometheus_target, execute_prometheus_instant_query all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so error-rate, request-rate, latency and any DB/connection-pool metric series for payment-api are unknown rather than zero, and no alert state could be read.

Jaeger was unreachable (traces_list_services and traces_search for service 'payment' returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so which downstream dependency or database call failed and whether error spans exist on payment-api cannot be established; no parent-child call edge is claimed.

Two Loki queries returned status no_data: {namespace="app-259"} excluding 'Payment processed successfully' and 'Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted' over 2026-11-23T11:00:00Z-16:28:00Z (view 390a74ba-dc0c-41be-848c-14ca371d64de-t0:4fdf288a-f5c8-4cd4-b56b-bfb017e0c3ed), and {namespace="app-259"} filtered on start/listen/ready/shutdown/terminat/restart/health/version/initializ in the same window (view 390a74ba-dc0c-41be-848c-14ca371d64de-t1:9c0748a3-e65d-4b82-8fbd-d5a7d1d6054f). Both matched nothing; that is not proof that no such lines, startup records or restarts exist.
Loki contained only the payment-api stream in namespace app-259; no database, proxy or platform component logs were available, and the database identity and pool size/limit values remain unknown.
Change history is not an integrated source in this Run, so whether any deployment or ConfigMap change occurred just before 13:46 UTC could not be verified.
Downstream/caller impact (for example checkout or customer-facing failures) was not observed in any available source and is therefore unverified.
Whether the payment-api pod or container restarted or was reconfigured around 13:46-14:44 UTC is unknown; logs alone cannot settle it.
next_steps: Re-run the Kubernetes reads (pod status/conditions, container restart counts and last termination, events across all namespaces, Deployment/ReplicaSet ownership) once the cluster source is reachable, to see whether the pod restarted or was rolled out around 13:46-14:44 UTC.
Read the payment-api ConfigMap/Deployment environment for database pool settings (max pool size, acquire timeout) and compare with the observed queue_length 5-15 and wait_time_ms up to 4840.

Query Prometheus error-rate and latency for service payment-api over 13:30-15:00 UTC, plus any database/connection-pool metrics, once Prometheus is reachable, and compare against a pre-13:46 baseline.
Query Jaeger traces for the failing payment operations in 13:46-14:44 UTC to identify the dependency or database call that held connections, and check that dependency's own error signals.
Check the database dependency's health and saturation (connections in use, max connections, slow queries) over 13:40-14:50 UTC.
Check the platform change history for any rollout or configuration change to payment-api or its database shortly before 13:46 UTC.
